newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Petrobras stops paying suppliers - agency.
newsitem.headline: Petrobras stops paying suppliers - agency.

text.p: Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras has stopped paying sugar and alcohol producers in the states of Sao Paulo and Pernambuco due to cash-flow problems, news agency InvestNews reported.

"Petrobras is suffering from a serious cash-flow problem because it is buying alcohol at higher prices than it is selling it for," the agency quoted Fernando Viana, superintendent of the company's legal division, as saying.
"This is strongly pressuring the company's cash-flow and in some instances we are delaying payments," he told InvestNews.

Petrobras had still not been refunded by the Treasury for 4.2 billion reais ($4 billion) in state subsidies to alcohol prices which it paid out in 1996 and this was causing the current problems, the lawyer added.
Company officials were not immediately available to comment.
Petrobras will appeal against a Sao Paulo court ruling condemning it to pay 150 million reais in fines for late payment to 131 Sao Paulo industries, Viana said.
